evidence.quote: I went back and forth, ended up shortlisting Vendor A.

evidence.quote: Vendor A's deck opened with a stat — 98% of their enterprise migrations completed without a reported incident. Vendor B's numbers came through an analyst report... A follow-up technical call later clarified those were actually describing the same rate.
evidence.explanation: The participant actively gathers, compares, and later verifies vendor-supplied statistics from multiple sources.

evidence.quote: I posted in a regional admin group, and the response was pretty clear — five of six comparable firms in our sector had already gone with Vendor A's platform.

evidence.quote: Looking back, those earlier cutovers were on architecture I already knew well. This was a genuinely different authentication model, and I didn't really weigh that difference when I made the call.
evidence.explanation: The participant forms a generalized model comparing prior technical environments to the new one, diagnosing why the analogy failed — an abstraction/diagnosis operation beyond raw information gathering.

evidence.quote: "98% success" sounds a lot more solid than "2% incident rate," even though — yeah, in hindsight those are the same number.
evidence.explanation: The task requires interpreting, comparing, and converting numerical/statistical figures (CVSS score, success/incident percentages) to inform a decision.

evidence.quote: a critical remote-code-execution CVE in our concentrator's firmware — a 9.8 on the CVSS scale
evidence.explanation: Interpreting a standardized numerical severity score is a numeracy task directly used to gauge urgency.

evidence.quote: Migration got approved, and we scheduled the cutover.
evidence.explanation: The participant coordinates a multi-step migration involving staffing, vendor engagement, and scheduling, implying organizational coordination of dependencies, though direct evidence of managing other people's work is limited (small two-person team).

evidence.quote: That was very much in my head when I was explaining to leadership why we needed to move fast on the patch specifically.
